title: The objective is empire benefit
statement: CSC AI should use worthwhile, durable supply chains to support empire needs, priorities and victory progress. Fewer good chains may beat more weak commitments. Both Basic and RH profiles share this objective; strategic Service selection remains an eventual capability.
scope: Confirmed project direction, 28 October, through the latest closed studies.
limits: District counts, subsidies, Service flags and isolated functioning chains do not establish the full objective. Sustained multi-map Basic/RH competence and net benefit remain unproved.

title: The true baseline excludes CSC AI aids
statement: The agreed baseline retains real CSC gameplay and only the shared resource-generation pass. It excludes private AI cues, Builder tuning, research guidance, paid acquisition and injected foundations. Disabling an external planner alone does not create it. RH-only is a separate underlying-AI reference, not stock AI.
scope: The formal comparison contract accepted 22 October.
limits: Historical tuned controls, saved-world counterfactuals and old resource-pass versions must retain their actual labels. Verify initial maps and loaded actions, not seeds alone.

title: Early baselines exposed distinct bottlenecks
statement: Five Standard-speed turn 200 games contained 175 major-city observations and 188 completed Quarters, only five with both owned material classes. Bakers had 130 mills,14 Bakeries and no Cafes; Tailors had four Workshops. The later ten Online 250 games contained 598 major-city observations and 776 Quarters, only six retaining Both. These are different clocks and samples.
scope: Five October 15 Standard games and ten October 16–17 Online vanilla/TAR games.
limits: Descriptive baselines are not causal tests. Owned plot-legal alternatives were scanned up to one turn earlier and did not establish affordability or complete production eligibility. Tailor Both-choice denominators were particularly small.

title: Both potential is not working supply
statement: Base can support Stage 2/3 Services; Both is especially valuable for Stage 4 potential. Ownership and adjacency do not prove valid improvements, producers, customers or timely operation. Ordinary sales can operate without material or Service-civic gates, and partial material/producer benefits can precede a full-chain milestone.
scope: Mechanic-specific measurements across historical experiments and November source.
limits: A nonoperating full-supply commitment is not automatically zero return or waste. Structural links and Service properties are not logged monetary payments.

title: Measure conversion, durability and trade-offs
statement: Use fixed opportunity definitions, absolute operating counts and city/population context. Separate native/assisted origins, site ages, own funds/subsidies, losses, repairs and supply-turns. Compare overall empire development and displaced investment as well as conversion efficiency.
scope: Common evaluation framework, rather than a single profit formula.
limits: Games are independent sampling units; five players from one map are not five worlds. Late investments are censored, zero opportunities are not zero success, and missing telemetry remains unknown.

title: More resources do not ensure useful city opportunities
statement: Fifteen paired native maps showed TAR Abundant mostly redistributing sites, while Truly Abundant increased Both-site counts. Some paired maps lacked Tailor specialty resources entirely. Offline studies and native helper follow-ups developed a resource-generation pass; production scope narrowed to Bakers/Tailors and temporary Tailor density assistance increased opportunities.
scope: Five paired landscapes, historical 80-layout emulator study and separate native helper/density samples.
limits: Geographic counts precede ownership, city reach, visibility, research and complete legality. Fixed-landscape emulation does not reproduce all native RNG/start adjustment. Shared clusters are not independent investments, and map assistance is not AI competence.

title: Early co-location gains did not solve material choice
statement: Placement v 1 increased Quarter/customer co-location without convincing mapped-material improvement and with more supporting deposits covered later. The subsequent native bonus/river package chose Bakers Base in 24/27 opportunities versus 14/25 baseline and 16/28 v 1 on one seed.
scope: Historical combined treatments, including one completed Online 250 bonus/river game.
limits: One seed and multiple changed inputs cannot isolate each cue or establish general superiority. Better placement still needs retained supply and development.

title: The broad BONUS cue was effective but poorly targeted
statement: The generic bonus-resource proxy changed native values and siting, but rewarded resources unmapped to the relevant Quarter. In density-v 4, nine of eleven Tailors beside bonus resources had only wrong-industry bonus types. Later mechanism contrasts confirmed responsiveness without a demonstrated chain-quality improvement; current source removes BONUS 12.
scope: Historical proxy experiments and current November source.
limits: Removing it is not itself proved to improve the economy. Broader guidance can incidentally help, so removal and exact-material replacement require their own outcome evidence.

title: Markers and resource-class sets were rejected representations
statement: Synthetic feature markers reached prospective native previews but accumulated clearing, placement and presentation side effects. A separate custom resource-class probe worked, while tested list encodings behaved as single distinct class identifiers. Resource reclassification would change gameplay and cannot cleanly represent overlapping CSC TypeTags.
scope: October 17 marker trial and October 28 native resource-class probes.
limits: Preview recognition does not establish safe metadata or better natural choices. The tested class encodings failed multiple membership; do not infer arbitrary parser capabilities from a TEXT column.

title: Spatial amounts and preferences have different units
statement: Ordinary native adjacency with dynamic private yields reaches district valuation. Yield bias 25 is a percentage-style contribution; the traced positive Districts preference uses aggregate sign and a 1.5 multiplier. Raw private yield is not that many final score points.
scope: Current-build static consumers and bounded runtime mechanism contrasts.
limits: Costs, time discount, competing land value and caches intervene. The two final observer diagnostics captured no target Quarter decision and closed after excessive callback fan-out; no calibrated placement benefit follows.

title: Broad Builder tuning had mixed confounded outcomes
statement: The historical 90/900 package reached improvement density 7.76/city versus 5.22 at the common 200 checkpoint, but did not finish 250. A later resource-layout variant with the same settings gave 6.70/city at 200. Training, purchases, unit additions and remaining charges measure different things. Later native tracing established that the Units-list Value adds to request priority rather than acting like a percentage; Basic's Builder 50 is not a promise of 50 workers. Required City=-1 removes one city-ID restriction while retaining ordinary eligibility checks; it does not assign a worker or guarantee recruitment.
scope: One-seed historical Builder/density trials and current-build static Units/request consumer tracing.
limits: Interrupted runs do not enter completed 250 comparisons. Combined settings and changed worlds do not identify a useful individual coefficient or prove sufficient workers for a particular job.

title: Private yields are not human-economically inert
statement: Zero-turn readbacks showed one worker move to Flax with private+40, changing ordinary worked Production/Culture despite unchanged real plot inputs. The later Plantation extension changed allocations/output without additional material development. Empty icons and UI filters do not prevent this.
scope: All-owner raw-resource/improvement mechanism arms.
limits: No direct conversion into money does not imply no economic effect. Older inert-output wording is superseded; all-owner diagnostic packages were not AI-only release candidates.

title: Soft care landed without reliable preservation
statement: Material-care v 1 stopped 170; v 2 ended after observer defeat 192 rather than 225. V 2 recorded eleven repair-to-working episodes and thirteen supporting-link losses, including four confirmed native harvests for Farm jobs. A working improvement was sometimes actively removed before harvesting.
scope: Historical 160/80/20 care and urgency experiments.
limits: Occupancy alone is not a confirmed harvest. Repairs do not prove incentive causality, and nodeSUCCESS is not operation/completion. Neither endpoint achieved the declared 225 test.

title: A harvest ban was an unsuitable preservation control
statement: The no-harvest rule prevented the raw control’s three losses through 75 and yielded six versus five working Base producers. It also removed Quarter options and caused repeated rejected harvest/build routes, some later adapting to Pastures.
scope: Identical source 16→75 counterfactual pair.
limits: One world, shared private signals and subsidies; zero working Both producers. A player-wide legality restriction is not targeted care and was not promoted.

title: Direct Pasture and conditional Farm routes had positive controls
statement: Cattle 2533 changed from a Farm reservation/harvest in the raw control to a Pasture reservation 20, working 21 and retained 75 under direct Pasture 80. The 150 resource-Farm pilot verified seven isolated resource-Farm positives and 81 terrain-only negatives, with logged job/reservation and physical development evidence.
scope: Separate historical direct and conditional forecasting treatments.
limits: All-owner scope, whole-bundle/timing differences and divergent spending prevent isolated empire-benefit claims. The Farm poweroff left 45 research rows and other interval observations missing; its dense-observation pass stayed false. Preservation and repeated pillage remained problems.

title: District-free supply is necessary but insufficient
statement: A planner falsely counted Silk retained under a City Center as future Plantation supply. The corrected same-source 75 guard omitted that site: four valid foundations versus five, unchanged seven working Base producers and zero Both producers.
scope: Exact precommit audit and external planner/commit correction.
limits: A globally valid improvement mapping plus owned/revealed/district-free resource does not prove current unlock, terrain legality, reachable Builder or eventual work. Fewer false starts is a quality fix, not a causal whole-mod victory.

title: Recommendations, assignments and getter domains differ
statement: Honey became its city’s highest returned recommendation at 112/113 and stayed unimproved; different Builders received identical city lists. Flax’s absence did not prove illegality or zero hidden value. Separate probes also found existing serialized Farm values and newly assigned Sugar responding differently despite correct loaded definitions.
scope: Bounded follow-through, recommendation/admission and zero-turn delivery studies.
limits: No same-path positive control means a getter’s zero is inconclusive. UI, Gameplay, initialization phase and reload cannot be interchanged; recommendation is not admitted work or allocated capacity.

title: Following did not establish dynamic civic consumption
statement: Clean sham/stock-Naval/custom-CSC arms had 400 identical civic-history rows each through 150 and 59 natural completion boundaries per arm. Retrospective analysis matched 5002 candidate keys per arm, including 327 Naval keys. No logged target-score or choice response was observed.
scope: One synthetic Medieval-start fixture with five AI players; earlier 180/120 and fixed/extreme controls provide supporting history.
limits: The planned Culture-weight positive sample was unavailable, not a measured zero. These are bounded route nulls without a working positive control, not proof that all civic preferences fail. Failed research-clearing assumptions and residual lists remain documented.

title: Trait preferences and construction goals worked separately
statement: Trait-owned favoring raised a target civic score about 50% in the tested context. A temporary construction prerequisite delivered PresentValue-sized research boosts: four of five selected and three completed Divine Right versus zero in the disconnected arm.
scope: Disposable matched Medieval mechanism controls, not ordinary CSC Service dependencies.
limits: The typed target came from an artificial prerequisite. Safe material-aware goal ownership, submission and complete withdrawal were not established. Callback tables lacked a player ID in the captured generic Lua-condition calls.

title: Dormant forecasts delivered selective research value
statement: A contradictory economically inactive CivicModifiers benefit plus private Yield strategy produced boosts for material-ready Tailors and zero for no-Quarter/no-Base controls. Exit variants withdrew value, but finite C 11/C 12 probes did not regain the treatment after supply recovery.
scope: Controlled civic-modifier diagnostics; actual Service effects were unchanged.
limits: Diagnostic magnitudes are not recommended weights. UI/human effects, complete lifecycle and natural-game benefit were not release-qualified; repeated arbitrary flag or weight changes were stopped.

title: Permanent restart failure was an overgeneralization
statement: Later natural guidance showed Germany’s Feudalism/Faires and Greece’s Urbanization re-adopted 20 turns after stopping. This supersedes a blanket irreversible-strategy interpretation while preserving the earlier finite no-restart observations.
scope: Two qualifying Game 1 return episodes; Games 2/3 lacked equivalent recovery opportunities.
limits: Twenty turns is an observed delay, not a universal cooldown or a complete lifecycle fix. Continued callbacks, adoption, preference application and score consumption remain distinct.

title: Research adoption did not establish chain improvement
statement: Three Ancient candidates completed 3735 observations; all 15 AI completed five lower Service civics and six completed Opera. Nine Naval completions lacked direct Naval eligibility. Separately, the long paired test ended with 12 Service flags versus 18 OFF.
scope: Three natural candidates and a separate Medieval 250 pair.
limits: Candidate/historical comparisons changed source and resource versions; the long pair’s OFF retained legacy guidance. Research gates often stopped being the endpoint bottleneck because materials, producers and venues did not align.

title: Boolean strategies are not per-plot score callbacks
statement: Call Lua Function can compute a complex accessible-state condition and switch linked player-level preferences. It does not itself transmit a candidate city/plot or continuous numeric desirability. Source registration and Following do not prove consumption by every downstream subsystem.
scope: Shipped API pattern, current CSC strategy use and traced consumer distinctions.
limits: An arbitrary numerical placement formula needs a separately proved consumer. UI previews and plot-property writers alone do not establish native hypothetical evaluation.

title: Private producer value reached an unbuilt Workshop decision
statement: A bounded trace captured a legal unbuilt Textile Workshop’s fresh NetValue and nested private getter 80, later best-building selection and queue entry. This is stronger than a UI preview or loaded row.
scope: Historical Kobdo 110/111 RH package and current-build native consumer investigation.
limits: The OFF arm never ran. Delivery, consumption and one choice do not prove 80 caused that choice, completion or economic benefit. Today’s population/property-consumer source is not the historical package.

title: Accepted work can wait behind another queue
statement: The exact target district request was accepted 103/105 while Builder production continued, selected/Execute at 109 when the queue emptied, and completion-censored at 110. Native construction can use a prepared foundation without an immediate queue replacement.
scope: Single-target existing-city observation and static contract trace.
limits: Priority, PresentValue, retained contract value, best-building fallback and final queue arbitration differ. No general finish-first override was proved.

title: Strategy building inputs loaded without the hoped response
statement: Twenty-seven CSC counterparts added to RH strategy Buildings lists had verified definitions/adoption but V 7’s physical state, finance and scoped construction/strategy/tree logs matched V 6 through 150. A conditional Granary strategy later reported true/Following while the observed ordinary building path still received preference 0.
scope: Fixed-A RH package comparison and separate bounded Granary delivery probe.
limits: These are route/context non-responses, not unsupported Buildings everywhere or proof that another Value increase would help. Specialization probes also lacked a responsive positive control.

title: Direct Granary preference worked without controlling the target
statement: Direct trait binding delivered preference 1 in 20/20 captured evaluations and two exact 2× Granary winners. The prescribed city still lacked Granary/Bakery after 21 intervals; Choir elsewhere completed Granary and began Bakery. Its Food 2 versus database base 1 is compatible with an additional CSC effect.
scope: Genghis trait-wide experimental 110→131 control.
limits: Instrumentation/recovery differences prevent isolated causality; Walls and military allocation changed. The wider gain was not free, and Choir lacked a full retained-chain material/effect census.

title: Customer geometry was a concrete repeated failure
statement: All four selective-assisted sites had working Both and upstream producers at 150 but no operating customer path. Three lacked Stage 2 geography; Choir had an adjacent City Center without Granary. All four also lacked registered Stage 3 customer geometry.
scope: Four precisely identified assisted investments in the selective RH screen.
limits: More Both starts alone would not address the diagnosed customer-path gap. Partial extraction/producer benefits do not require the full operating milestone, so these cases are not automatically zero-income.

title: Current future inputs are explicitly authored
statement: An existing Tailors Quarter supplies Workshop private 80 for BASE plus 40 with SPEC. The RH role bridge does not itself check Quarter completion/pillage. An existing functioning Bakers Mill can target Granary private 40 before Granary exists; the real Mill→Granary exchange instead requires actual recipient Granary.
scope: Pinned November 3 source and native analysis.
limits: Fact flags use mapped-resource presence, ownership, reveal and district-free checks, not full improvement buildability or Builder availability. Do not describe historical getter 80 as a run of the whole current source tree or evidence of complete native network simulation.

title: Current population returns are realized-state calculations
statement: Stage 3 per-population seller/customer consumers attach to City Centers; Lua computes actual functioning same-owner adjacent relationships and writes bits. Stage 4/export consumers can instead adjust named building yields. Legacy producer-owned definitions can remain present but unattached.
scope: November 3 source, after consumer changes.
limits: Native unsupported collections, omitted property gates and missing plot context prevent assuming faithful arbitrary future-chain forecasting. Missing material is not equivalent to no ordinary Stage 3 sales.

title: Foundations can be handed to native construction
statement: The initial four-foundation diagnostic observed all four selected and completed without scripted completion or extra production orders. Later aged cohorts also completed most foundations; construction was often stronger than material siting/preservation.
scope: Guarded native/UI-legal incomplete district route.
limits: Foundation insertion consumes land and district capacity and changes the AI’s remaining choices. It proves a construction route in cases, not optimal investment or chain success.

title: Paid acquisition is an assisted backend
statement: A donated Both diagnostic verified 65 Gold in source/Sheep acquisitions, exact gift/debit, same-turn city ownership and a legal 0%Tailors foundation. Later own-first policies donate only the next step’s shortfall with receipts, caps, reserves and cooldowns.
scope: Gameplay WorldBuilder city assignment plus native-quoted treasury debit.
limits: This is not proved native AI PURCHASE behavior. A full-route gift or same-state affordability shadow is a mechanism diagnostic, not an untreated counterfactual or free-chain outcome.

title: Guaranteed Both placement did not retain most inputs
statement: In the partial 175 cohort all 11 assisted foundations completed, while 64/65 native placements completed. Only two assisted working Base/Both chains remained after nine initial Base losses. Captured sites and paid-land overlaps were tracked separately.
scope: Original-placement cohorts; later uncontrolled 192 excluded.
limits: Unassisted does not mean stock AI. Assistance preempted some Both choices, and cohort ages/opportunities differ; native-versus-assisted fractions are not causal treatment effects.

title: A partial200 package improved some milestones
statement: All 11 assisted foundations completed with mean observed delay 21/median 20 versus 28.125/27 for eight prior completions. Non-City-Center customer adjacency 31 versus 18 and building links 19 versus 8 rose, while working Base producer sites fell 15 versus 21.
scope: Historical combined foundation/customer treatment; controlled progress ended 175.
limits: The requested 200 endpoint was not completed. Observer defeat, unobserved later finance and changed cohorts prevent a full benchmark or isolated queue-priority efficacy claim.

title: Spending195 versus795 was not selective-chain success
statement: The selective candidate spent 195 Gold=81 own+114 subsidy versus 795=300+495, but ended with three full-supply contexts versus four. Both had 53 Quarters,19 workingBase and 38 Stage 2 producers; candidate Both was four versus ten and zero assisted sites operated.
scope: One matched 150 RH joint-package screen.
limits: Savings 75.5% is not benefit, parity or proof of lower waste. Full-chain milestone spending is not total return accounting; materials/producers may already help. Construction cost was not monetized.

title: Customer-aware v2 proved execution, not overall improvement
statement: V 2 admits credible Base through Both or trial realProduction+Gold>=4 and requires an exact Stage 2/3 customer path. Its 150 pilot had two full contexts versus three selective,15 Base versus 19, and one assisted chain operating from 119 through later observations. Five foundations were assisted, fifty sites clearly native and one had cross-city acquired-land overlap.
scope: Canonical implementation and same-map RH joint-package pilot.
limits: 200 Gold included 85 on a turn-149 commitment censored at 150. Sixteen errors and missing planner observations 11–14 kept the dense-observation pass false. An individual functioning chain did not establish overall improvement or Basic qualification.

title: Future customer credit needs a named conditional contract
statement: V 2 binds material/customer identities across purchases and protects essential footprints. Working customers, existing districts missing buildings and specific future plots are different confidence tiers. Present real P/G, projected conditional value and private cues stay separate.
scope: Customer-aware planner contract and Lua legality-binding investigation.
limits: CanHaveDistrict does not prove future unlock/capacity legality. Unknown essential facts defer action; unknown secondary costs remain explicit rather than making every useful investment impossible. Future promises are not native site preferences or realized yields.

title: Profile separation is architecture, not qualification
statement: Off means native CSC without CSC AI interventions, or RH alone when RH is active. On selects Basic or RH-specific support, with a separate subsidy option. Basic owns general Builder/improvement/movement/contract inputs; RH is intended to own its baseline while CSC addresses evidenced supply-chain gaps.
scope: Current objectives/source architecture and dated native pilots.
limits: A historical profile status or manifest is not current installed-state proof. No sustained multi-map Basic/RH competence or parity was established, and old global Builder weights must not be silently shared into RH.

title: RH version changes invalidate copied assumptions
statement: The old 4.34 reference used improvement 90/globalBuilder 900. Reviewed 5.097 uses improvement 30, no equivalent globalBuilder 900 row, +1 friendly movement and substantial Lua Builder purchasing. Selecting a needy spawn city is not dispatching an existing Builder to an exact resource job.
scope: Read-only, version-pinned RH source review.
limits: Leader overrides, load order and activation gates matter. RH’s separate resource-improvement fallback is a stronger intervention, not proof of a native job dispatcher. Reference source is read-only; source declarations are not performance validation.

title: AI+ and Real Strategy supplied bounded leads
statement: AI+ led to RequiredCity=-1 and AddGoalTech civic payload wiring. Real Strategy supplied trait/list and Lua-strategy precedents, while its historical system comments helped distinguish subsystem semantics. Their successful packages do not prove every named preference or current-build consumer works.
scope: Read-only AI+v 13, RealStrategy 2.3.1 and RH dynamic-research reviews.
limits: No arbitrary per-Quarter resource matcher or safe CSC Service-goal adapter emerged. Author-reported behavior remains separate from locally reproduced runtime results; civic preferences and ordinary yield percentages are not interchangeable units.

title: The RH parity campaign did not qualify a winner
statement: V 6 reached 150 with 57 cities,55 completedQuarters,39 producers,21 Base,5 Both,8 customer links and 4 flags, but failed its per-city and customer/Service gates against Basic-A. V 7’s 27 strategy additions matched V 6’s physical signature, scoped logs and finance through 150.
scope: Historical fixed-A RH development series, not three independent parity successes.
limits: Startup retries, same-world reloads and source candidates are not independent worlds. Later closures and the paused broad campaign override diary statements that say ACTIVE. Current source is not automatically the executed candidate.

title: Controls must share the getter and context
statement: Loaded rows and empty modifier subject lists do not establish delivery. UI/Gameplay getters can disagree, initialization phases differ and saved instances may retain earlier behavior. A responsive same-path positive control must precede interpreting a zero.
scope: Farm, acquisition, producer-property and general mechanism probes.
limits: Failed positive controls make route interpretation inconclusive. They do not prove a mechanism unsupported everywhere or justify arbitrary coefficient increases; isolate application before testing decisions.

title: Worlds, clocks and source generations must match
statement: Same seeds do not guarantee identical resources/starts across builds. Saved-world arms overlap; Medieval starts 71 and Online/Standard clocks differ. Preserve initial state, actual boundaries, exact executed packages and accepted log generations.
scope: Baseline, research, material, producer and planner comparisons.
limits: Never sum replays as independent outcomes, fill missing telemetry, compare historical pins against promoted source, or describe a post-closure repair as runtime validation. Cached advice, proposals and decisions have separate refresh timing.

title: Stall, save failure, host loss and native crash differ
statement: Disaster/diplomacy playback locks produced verified stalls; shipped UI release sometimes restored progress. Host shutdowns and optional-save failures preserved useful partial data without proving native crashes. One shared finite controller, identity-qualified owners and one-shot financial receipts improved reliability.
scope: Foundation-series recovery, harness and shared-session/exit investigations.
limits: A missing reply or vanished worker is not a cause diagnosis. Acknowledgment is not completed effect; ambiguous economy must not be resent. Repair reporting offline rather than rerunning worlds for missing fields.

title: Instrumentation cost can defeat the question
statement: Two placement diagnostics produced 882774 and 294437 callbacks in one AI interval, captured no target Quarter decision and closed normally. Moving hooks did not solve fan-out; no weight treatment followed. Native-side filtering before the JavaScript boundary became the prerequisite for future instrumented captures.
scope: Bounded November 1 observer branch, current Windows build.
limits: This is a measurement-budget failure, not AI blindness, a successful calibration or permission for a third retry. The broad optimisation campaign remains paused.

title: Reverse engineering should resolve dependencies
statement: PE checks, reference names, Ghidra and REA clarified consumers, ownership and side effects. Economic goal feasibility stopped at an unestablished arbitrary payload/ownership interface; planner work could continue through supported guidance and guarded acquisition/foundations.
scope: Native tooling and economic-job feasibility work.
limits: Names and historical layouts are leads. A scripted operation setter can mutate AI knowledge before invalid-ID validation, so invalid ID is not a safe no-effect control. No universal executor, complete reconstruction or token-savings gain was established.

title: The full objective remains unproved
statement: Useful acquisition, fresh value delivery, native selections, repairs, completions and individual functioning chains are demonstrated. Reliable sustained operation, balanced opportunity cost and net benefit across Basic/RH and multiple maps remain open.
scope: Latest audited project checkpoint plus November 3 source/native work.
limits: Old diaries may say ACTIVE or pending. Latest human stops, audit closures and paused campaigns prevail. These pages are knowledge, not active jobs, release qualification or authority to start a game/monitor.

title: A fresh offline evaluator exposes conditional Tailors investment rankings
statement: An independent Tailors review model evaluates 44 copied historical cases: six new-site alternatives and38 existing Quarters. It compares building bundles with retain/defer, separates yield/cost/timing ledgers, preserves material/customer gates and unknowns, and provides27 assumption scenarios plus priced future-customer branches.
scope: First Tailors mechanics profile, current workspace source pins and four closed capture hashes.41 partial numerical reviews; three unfinished Quarters need remaining-production inputs. The six new sites have no owned mapped supply. Kerma's modeled Fashion House investment changes with horizon/cost assumptions. No game, installed content or native score was changed.
limits: Partial review utility is not native Q8, actual profit, a bound on benefit or a deployed policy. Earlier treatments remain part of the captured worlds. Services, trade, specialists, growth, competing uses, queue delays and other effects remain unpriced; unsupported Quarters/integrations and native-overlap conversion need further work. Conditional future paths are not observed completions or permission to act.

title: A full-adjacency +4 policy delivers promoted Bakers sites while other sites remain selectable
statement: A fresh per-turn Bakers/Tailors policy reuses loaded adjacency rules, includes rivers and the appropriate planned first Bakers Mill, and promotes the highest qualifying Production+Gold >=4 pair per original-AI city. In a recovered Online-speed game ending at100,52 fresh native additions reached9 Best returns covering7 distinct promoted Bakers pairs; all7 later founded and completed. Another23 Quarters founded below4 in their preceding scans.
scope: One CSC-only Ancient/Prince/Small Continents world, original AI1–5. Machine interruption after accepted5; archived autosave6 recovered with original identities/preferences. Accepted scans1–100,95 finalized native windows,0 native errors, normal game/daemon exit0 and installed content/preferences verified. All qualifying pairs were Bakers; Tailors never reached4.
limits: No matched untreated control, caused-choice-change claim, release carrier, first-Mill construction incentive or economic-benefit proof. Other sites are not banned. Prior-scan adjacency is not exact construction-tick value. Conditional Mill bonus is not immediate income or a building grant. Removing a table entry does not roll back caches/requests. Timing is coarse, not a CPU benchmark.

title: A signed native extension can discourage individual weak Quarter sites
statement: The v2 adjacency policy retains the best >=4 pair promotion and supplies graded negative adjustments for every observed sub-4 Bakers/Tailors pair. A recovered Online100 game recorded13881 deductions,75 additions and0 native errors in completed windows;10 promoted and4 below-4 Quarters founded,12 completed. Two weak sites entered native requests before scanner coverage; two remained positive after deduction and won after downstream valuation. This demonstrates a working soft deduction and specific escape paths, not a universal exclusion.
scope: Exact pinned XP2, one CSC-only Ancient/Prince/Small Continents Online world. Controller handoff exception after80; preserved save80 recovered with exact captured scanner facts, installed/dependency/preferences equality. Accepted scans1-100, partial original80-to81 window separate.10 promoted foundations include2 Tailors;9 promoted completed.20 policy/recovery tests,40 real-kernel host checks,9 scanner checks,161 controller checks and35 Lua fixtures after repair. Final native/daemon exit0 and preferences restored.
limits: No matched untreated control or economic-benefit proof;23-to4 weak-foundation comparison is descriptive. Scanner parity is not full-world/RNG/cache/fractional-turn parity. Priority amounts are not calibrated utility. Native zero/invalid values and conservative floor remain protected. Exact early scanner-exclusion cause unrecorded. No request rollback, first-Mill incentive or release integration. No negative Best winner observed in this game, although static signed comparison allows one.

title: RH5 uses custom adjacency incentives rather than a visible native score hook
statement: Installed RH5.097 defines positive and negative district adjacencies using RH_YIELD_LAST_RESORT, including reciprocal Industrial Zone/infrastructure relationships. This implements general placement-score steering through SQL. No direct native district-score hook was found in the reviewed package; CSC's prototype can instead supply independently calculated signed per-pair adjustments.
scope: Read-only4 November2026 installed Workshop3792072489, manifest5.097, RH_Districts.sql, RH_Improvements.sql, complete file inventory and bounded Lua/SQL searches. No game, attachment or tuning change.
limits: Source establishes technique and intent, not measured runtime efficacy or the author's complete knowledge. Package absence cannot exclude external or unpublished tooling. Custom yield amounts and bias fields are not measured Q8 additions. Older public-source yield identifiers differ.

title: The existing v2 Quarter policy now runs in packaged Lua through CE
statement: The Lua port preserves the current best Production+Gold >=4 Bakers/Tailors promotion and graded weak-site deduction, reuses the same river/conditional first-Mill scanner, and excludes original humans and already-founded city/types. Each of two CE-carried Online100 tests has101 matching Lua/Python plans. The earlier test recorded73 additions/14584 deductions and12 AI Quarter foundations,11 complete. The supported develop/MSVC regression separately recorded62 additions/13746 deductions with the reviewed adjacency files.
scope: Unchanged csc-adjacency-policy-v2, CSC-only Ancient/Prince/Small Continents/Online, original AI1–5. Each test has101 comparisons including duplicated saved6,100 publication windows, all four trace kinds/both signs/zero native faults/context/save/load/restoration. Shared controller, no district orders, grants or external policy publication. The develop regression uses a distinct CSC copy with four reviewed adjacency files; it is not a matched comparison with the earlier Core.
limits: Policy/intervention and diagnostic parity, not identical historical timing/outcomes or improved AI quality. Owned legal candidate scope and known native early-admission/retained-request gaps remain. Mill forecast is not a grant or building incentive.12 foundations/11 completions are observations, not caused completions or net benefit. No RH/multiplayer or stock-CE release claim.

statement: In a read-only recalculation of the archived weak-site world through81, Delhi's admitted Wind Mill1356033 plus Bakery1118 exactly added1357151 Q8 to positive Bakers rows; Majapahit Wind1589150 plus Bakery1023 and Cafe1640 added1591813. Water excluded by lower-index mutual canonicalization; hidden flags MustPurchase-excluded. Normal exit0,152 preference entries and content restored/verified.
limits: Recalculation in a prior treated world, not historical86/89 replay or an untreated/control comparison. No scoring repair, choice improvement, native-generation API, economic benefit or release/general compatibility established. limits: One city and one pair of continuations. Exact unit and project gate operands were captured only in the control. The earlier nomination used a diagnostic adjustment whose amount has not been generalised.

title: Integrated CSC and CE reproduced the Melbourne Wind Mill nomination and Service
statement: CSC published a bounded preference for the ready chain. CE increased the ordinary Wind Mill nomination from 93359 to 208047 Q8 once, and the native offer, construction and active Storekeeper followed without an external score writer.

Native contract 2391 carried the Mill on 132, started on 135, completed on 137, and Storekeeper operated on the measured turn 138. The matched no-bid replay with the same reviewed DLL carried Amphitheater.
limits: One saved city and a one-turn integrated payout window. The bounded 448-unit preference is an initial fixture calibration. Water Mill behavior, wider balance, mature-game overhead and fresh-start repeatability remain open.

title: Ancyra's Granary lost ordinary nomination and its open production slot went to Cuirassier
statement: Ancyra could build the Granary but it lost two ordinary comparisons to Castle. An already offered Cuirassier won the observed production opening. No Granary offer reached that queue gate.
scope: Read-only turn-139 to turn-150 continuation of AI-C093. Ancyra had an adjacent working Rice Farm and Feudalism but neither Granary nor Mill. The two Castle margins were 148034 and 120844 Q8.
limits: One city and a short interval. The measured margins do not value the two-building investment or prove how a Granary offer would compete at another opening.

title: Trebizond's Granary lost ordinary nomination to Library with a working Water Mill present
statement: The legal Granary reached the ordinary nomination at 46458 Q8. Library won at 119277 Q8 and became offer 3238. Earlier production openings accepted Star Fort and Theater Square contracts.
scope: Read-only turn-150 to turn-164 continuation of AI-C094. Trebizond had the working Water Mill and adjacent City Center with Granary available. Its Wheat remained unimproved at the start.

title: A matched Trebizond nomination produced a valid Granary offer at its native cache value
statement: A one-shot preference increased the ordinary Granary comparison from 46458 to 120186 Q8. Granary replaced Library in offer 3238, which validated at 46336 Q8.

title: Trebizond's nominated Granary was purchased through the admitted contract

scope: Read-only repeat of the turn-164 source from AI-C097 to the turn-167 exchange snapshot, before the later Mill damage.

statement: Four read-only BuildingValue calls admitted all four Granary-owned Mill yield roots and returned zero for each. The intrinsic Food normalization and native income stream imply about 18–19 utility units for one additional Food in that case.

title: The calibrated Granary Food bid reached the native nomination while Library still won
statement: The clean CE replay logged the exact 4608 Q8 addition to Trebizond's Granary, from 46458 to 51066 Q8. The city submitted the same Library offer as in the control.
scope: Exact turn-150 replay through 164 with the pinned reviewed CE, integrated CSC policy, bounded packet logging and no external attachment.
limits: One native comparison in one saved city. The policy delivered its Food term and preserved the competing choice. It has not yet changed an ordinary-start Granary selection or verified a live unique replacement.

title: Native Production and Gold weights support a 52-point initial bid for the ordinary Granary exchange
statement: Same-player intrinsic yield references put one Production and one Gold at about 17.5 points each in the observed Granary income window. Together with the Food term, the initial rounded CSC bid is 52 points.
scope: Read-only repeat of AI-C100 from turn 150 to 154. Sixteen positive inputs of each yield used the same player valuation object. The Granary's own income timing supplies the common 12.06 factor.
limits: One player's strategic weights and one income window. The calibrated bid is a coarse preference for an existing working Mill, with no deferred benefit or live unique-replacement claim.

title: The complete 52-point exchange preference reached native Granary nomination
statement: The packaged CSC policy and reviewed CE changed Trebizond's Granary from 46458 to 59770 Q8. Library kept the same native offer. Passive dependency snapshots completed at turns 153 and 160.
scope: Exact turn-150 Trebizond checkpoint to 164 with the 52-point CSC policy and no external attachment. CE recorded the exact city and building key.

title: Melbourne bought its nominated Wind Mill and activated Storekeeper from a normal start
statement: Integrated CE applied the 448-point Wind Mill nomination preference in Melbourne. Native production chose a Knight and then an Industrial Zone during earlier offers. The AI bought Wind Mill offer 1907 on turn 113, and the native Storekeeper attachment and Growth recipient were active from turn 114.
scope: One ordinary Small Continents development seed with frozen CSC and CE packages, stock AI, no external score writer and strict native effect samples through turn 154.
limits: No same-package no-bid arm for this run. The evidence establishes delivery, a purchase and realised Service, with no causal estimate or general calibration of 448 points.

title: Launceston received the full Granary exchange bid, bought the Granary and activated Storekeeper
statement: In an ordinary-start development game, Launceston bought a Water Mill on 181. The full 13312 Q8 exchange bid changed its Granary candidate from 78805 to 92117 Q8 in the next nomination interval. It bought the resulting offer on 188 and first operated Storekeeper on 189.
scope: One ordinary Small Continents development seed with integrated CSC and CE, exact nomination and city contract receipts, and native attachment and Growth recipient samples.
limits: One city and no matched no-bid arm. The sequence proves live delivery and follow-through. It cannot establish that the bid changed the winner. Activation was too late for 100 active turns by the endpoint.

title: Heidelberg repaired its Maize Farm and regained Storekeeper in an ordinary game
statement: Heidelberg first operated Storekeeper on 178. It was inactive on 184–186. The native improvement tree moved a Builder to its Maize tile and reported a successful Farm repair on 185. Native Storekeeper resumed on 187 for the same Quarter and City Center.
scope: One ordinary Small Continents development seed. The exact plot reservation, native repair and realised Growth effect are recorded by independent logs.
limits: The damage source was not identified. This is a supplier repair through the ordinary AI and does not isolate a treatment effect or cover Mill or Granary damage.

title: Heidelberg's Dam removed its only Maize supplier despite the district-score deduction
statement: The native district policy deducted 24576 Q8 from Heidelberg's Dam on its only adjacent Maize tile, including a change from 482672 to 458096 Q8. The city queued the Dam at that location on 206. Storekeeper stopped on 207 and the endpoint census confirmed the Dam and absence of Maize.
scope: One ordinary Small Continents development game with a working Heidelberg chain before Dam contract 4536. Exact CE pair, native contract and plot logs, physical censuses and continuous Service samples identify the loss.
limits: No matched control or counterfactual ranking of other Dam sites. The finite deduction demonstrably allowed this loss. The evidence does not establish the next best site or the correct replacement policy.

statement: The integrated Builder preference raised Melbourne's exact Rice Farm candidate from 18012 to 32348 Q8. The ordinary improvement tree reserved the tile on 239 and built a Farm on 241. The native Storekeeper effect resumed on 242 after three inactive turns.
scope: One ordinary Small Continents development game. Turn-240 physical census, CE score receipt, exact improvement tree and restored native Service agree for player 4, city 131073 and supplier plot 1498.
limits: No matched no-bid arm. The logs verify delivery, legal rebuild and restored Service. They do not identify the source of the loss or establish that the preference changed the job choice.

statement: A Lua regression fixture reproduced two identical 13312 Q8 nomination entries for a legal Granary replacement adjacent to two working Bakers Mills. CSC now emits one entry. The reviewed CE already deduplicates identical keys before scoring, so the change removes redundant work and packet entries.
scope: Actual CSC publisher, policy and bridge executed under Lua 5.1 with two Quarters and a shared customer. Static cross-check of finish_nominations in reviewed CE commit abf5d58.
limits: Offline packet evidence. Live shared-customer choice and the separate marginal value of a second Mill remain unmeasured.

title: The same ordinary development setup delivered the Pasture in a divergent branch
statement: With the same seed and integrated 14336 Q8 supplier preference, the player 2 Quarter at 2311 received its Pasture on 118 and operated Storekeeper on 119–153 in a second start. The original turn-249 run never improved that Cattle.

limits: Same setup is not a matched intervention. The successful branch proves repeat live follow-through, not that the preference changed native ranking. The turn-154 scope guard skipped the native observer because the supplier already worked.

title: The Pasture won three open admissions before a Builder completed it
statement: Eleven of 15 ordinary proposal checks in Alexandria Troas found an existing tree. The first three open checks selected the exact Pasture. statement: Seven opening forecasts credited +1 Production and +1 Gold to the legal unbuilt Wind Mill through current city yield changes. The hypothetical Food-to-Granary root returned zero. title: Melbourne reserved a Farm before it could recruit a Builder
statement: The ordinary improvement tree selected a Farm on Melbourne's bare Rice, reserved its exact tile, and failed to recruit a Builder at each check from 106 through 111. One Builder contract was submitted to six cities. Melbourne passed receive validation at 76800 Q8 and kept producing Kōtoku-in without a queue comparison. The Rice was still bare on 112.
scope: Melbourne opening diagnostics -02 and -03, prepared turn-105 saves with a removed Rice Farm, working Granary and unbuilt Wind Mill. No diagnostic score writes or CSC ready-chain preference for Melbourne.
limits: Short window with native offer tracing scoped to Melbourne. It does not isolate the failed recruitment or show whether other cities revalidated and ranked the accepted offer when their queues reopened.

title: Melbourne's measured chain benefits left Castle ahead in the missing-Farm replay
statement: Using the city's observed Food surplus, same-player Engineer weights and Mill income window, Storekeeper's Growth and Engineer point add about 21 utility points. The full set of missing CSC effects is about 85 points under immediate Farm and Service readiness, below the observed Castle margin of 121–281 points.
scope: Read-only Melbourne turn-105 opening diagnostic -03 through 112. Uses loaded CSC effect amounts, city Food surplus 9, same-player Engineer normalization of 230 Q8 per point, and the observed 12-to-50-turn Mill window.
limits: Sensitivity calculation for this fixture with no delays or costs, the Farm worked, and the observed pre-Farm surplus. The inactive Storekeeper roots did not return a native score. The result does not set a universal Mill preference or price a different city.

title: Melbourne's Rice Builder offer lost nine valid queue comparisons
statement: All six Australian cities accepted the Rice Farm's Builder offer at 76800 Q8. It stayed at that value after nine successful revalidations and refreshes. Each city executed a higher offer. Adelaide chose a different Builder contract at 94976 Q8, the closest margin.

limits: One diagnostic with the Rice Farm removed. The competing Builder was queued for Sydney's Farm but had not completed by the endpoint. The reason the nearby Builder was unavailable remains unresolved.

title: Sydney and Canberra used the Builder before Melbourne could recruit it
statement: Builder 2752514 repaired Sydney's Farm, then Canberra reassigned it and built an Outback Station. It was already processed at each Rice check from 106 through 114 and marked for removal on 115. No Builder entered Melbourne's candidate pool on those ten calls.
scope: Melbourne read-only diagnostic -02 from 105 to 116. Exact Rice target at 18,20, joined controller changes to Sydney Farm at 19,22 and Canberra Outback Station at 12,13. Opening census found one Builder with one charge.
limits: One shared-worker conflict. Establishes availability and execution in this fixture. It does not show how to reorder work across cities or establish the marginal value of another Builder.
